scope_assessment.next_target: Exact ordinary Lee curvature must pair nonnegatively with every smooth positive Gauduchon test, or an actual compact strictly LCK negative-pairing example must be constructed.
limits: Bounded source research is not exhaustive literature verification.
Publisher-final version and some author sites were not retrieved.
Restricted geometric deformation premises were not independently reconstructed.
Earlier printed dimension restriction and later restatement without that restriction remain separate.
No full proof, independent proof reconstruction, original closure or new finished paper follows from process completion.

notes.summary: The exact P03 claim appears as an explicit Ornea–Verbitsky conjecture, not an unrestricted theorem, in the inspected 2024 primary paper.
notes.detailedSummary: Ornea–Verbitsky’s arXiv:2407.04623v2 identifies pseudoeffectivity of the ordinary Bott–Chern class represented by −d(Iθ) as conjectural. Conjecture 4.14 and Remark 4.16 formulate the corresponding positivity against arbitrary Gauduchon metrics. The text explicitly says the conjecture is unproved. Its restricted theorem does not establish P03.
notes.text:
Primary full text opened: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.04623 and https://arxiv.org/html/2407.04623v2, Liviu Ornea–Misha Verbitsky, “Balanced metrics and Gauduchon cone of locally conformally Kähler manifolds.” First submitted July 5, 2024; inspected revision August 7, 2024. The arXiv record, https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04623, records publication in IMRN 2025, issue 3, rnaf014. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04623))

The abstract specifies −d(Iθ). Definition 4.7, p. 11, uses ordinary Bott–Chern classes of closed positive (1,1)-currents. Conjecture 4.14 and Remark 4.16, p. 12, identify the arbitrary-Gauduchon degree assertion with pseudoeffectivity. The opening of p. 13 states: “We still don’t know how to prove Conjecture 4.14.” Remark 4.15 distinguishes arbitrary Gauduchon tests from the LCK-induced test. Thus the inspected full text does not prove unrestricted P03. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.04623))

notes.summary: The explicit form −d(Iθ) has P03’s sign, but printed dᶜ conventions are internally inconsistent and must not be imported mechanically.
notes.detailedSummary: With the authors’ stated action Iα=−α∘I on one-forms, Iλ=4πλᶜ_task, so −d(Iλ)=4πκλ. This positive factor preserves pseudoeffectivity. However, the 2024 printed formula dᶜ=IdI gives the opposite result on closed one-forms from the identity used later in Remark 4.15. The potential paper also prints an opposite-sign operator while using another conjugation in its proof. These are convention mismatches, not counterexamples.
notes.text:
Sources opened: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.04623v2, §1.1 and Remark 4.15; and https://arxiv.org/html/2112.03363v2, “Conventions” and the proof of Theorem 8.4. The former states Iη(X₁,…,Xₖ)=(−1)ᵏη(IX₁,…,IXₖ) and dᶜ=IdI; Remark 4.15 instead uses dᶜθ=−dθᶜ, with θᶜ=Iθ. The latter prints dᶜ=I⁻¹dI but its Theorem 8.4 proof uses IₖdIₖ⁻¹θ∞. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.04623v2))

Explicit translation, computed from the stated action: I acts by −i on (1,0)-covectors and +i on (0,1)-covectors. Hence Iλ=i(λ⁰¹−λ¹⁰)=4πλᶜ_task, and therefore −d(Iλ)=4πκλ. Locally λ=df, so κλ=−ddᶜ_task f. The consistent standard operator C=i(bar∂−∂)=4πdᶜ_task satisfies Cλ=−d(Iλ)=4πκλ and dC=2i∂bar∂=4πddᶜ_task. The latter normalization is also explicitly stated in Remark 2.2 of https://arxiv.org/html/2411.05595v2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.05595v2))

The mismatch can be checked without a literature premise: for λ=df, d(Iλ) is of type (1,1), on which I acts as the identity. Consequently the literally printed IdI sends λ to +d(Iλ)=−4πκλ, contradicting Remark 4.15’s identity. Likewise I⁻¹dI, with the stated action, equals −C. Use the explicit curvature form −d(Iθ), not an unreconciled occurrence of dᶜθ, to identify P03. Multiplication of ddᶜ by a nonzero constant does not change its image in ordinary Bott–Chern cohomology, but reversing the representative’s sign does change the positivity question. This audit does not assert that the substantive restricted results are false.

notes.summary: The inspected positive theorems retain potential/bimeromorphic-class restrictions; their deformation arguments provide no route covering every strict LCK manifold.
notes.detailedSummary: Theorem 4.17 of the 2024 paper assumes compactness, non-Kählerness, complex dimension greater than 3 as printed, and bimeromorphic relation to an LCK-with-potential, Oeljeklaus–Toma, or Kato manifold. Its proof passes nonnegative degrees through specified deformation families, then obtains strictness from a nonzero positive current. Theorem 8.4 of the Lee-classes paper assumes potential and dimension at least 3. Neither theorem removes those geometric restrictions.
notes.text:
Opened full text: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.04623v2, Theorem 4.17 and proof, pp. 13–14 of the PDF. Its hypotheses are compact non-Kähler LCK, complex dimension greater than 3, and bimeromorphic relation to one of three named classes: LCK with potential, Oeljeklaus–Toma, or Kato. The conclusion is positive Lee degree for every Gauduchon metric. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.04623v2))

The proof uses semipositive forms for Vaisman/OT examples; a blow-up description cited to [OV7]; smooth dependence of conformal Gauduchon representatives; potential-to-Vaisman deformation cited to [OV6, Theorem 16.21]; and Kato-to-blown-up-Hopf deformation cited to [K]. Continuity gives nonnegativity, not strict positivity; Step 4 uses duality and Lemma 3.2 to obtain strictness. The p. 13 screenshot confirms ≥ in the intermediate steps where text extraction displayed >. These external deformation and modification premises were not independently reconstructed here. Nothing in this proof supplies the required families for arbitrary LCK manifolds. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.04623))

A directly inspected dependency is https://arxiv.org/html/2112.03363v2 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.03363v2, Ornea–Verbitsky, “Lee classes on LCK manifolds with potential,” revision January 8, 2022, published Tohoku Math. J. 76(1), 105–125 (2024). Theorem 8.4, PDF pp. 24–25, assumes compact LCK with potential and complex dimension at least 3. A nonzero real functional μ annihilates the codimension-one real holomorphic-form subspace and satisfies μ([θ])>0. Then ξ is a Lee class of a potential structure exactly when μ(ξ)>0. The proof invokes Theorems 6.1, 7.3, 8.3 and Proposition 8.1. Its potential hypothesis is essential to the stated result; it is not an unrestricted pseudoeffectivity theorem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03363))

notes.summary: The later Lee–Gauduchon primary paper explicitly repeats unrestricted pseudoeffectivity as Conjecture 5.13.
notes.detailedSummary: The November 14, 2024 revision of arXiv:2411.05595 proves cone duality but still states the universal LCK assertion as a conjecture. Theorem 5.11 concerns only its listed known-example classes. That restatement omits the earlier theorem’s dimension bound, but still does not quantify over all LCK manifolds.
notes.text:
Opened: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05595, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.05595 and https://arxiv.org/html/2411.05595v2, Ornea–Verbitsky, “The Lee–Gauduchon cone on complex manifolds.” Submitted November 8, 2024; revised November 14, 2024. Ornea’s opened publication list records a 2025 Springer chapter, pp. 237–250. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05595))

Conjecture 5.13, PDF p. 12, reads: “The two-form dᶜθ is pseudoeffective on all compact LCK manifolds.” Theorem 5.11, p. 11, applies only to the preceding classes: blow-ups of potential manifolds, blow-ups of OT manifolds, and Kato manifolds. Unlike the earlier Theorem 4.17, this restatement prints no dimension bound; that difference must not be silently harmonized. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.05595))

Definition 2.1 uses ordinary Bott–Chern cohomology. Theorem 3.11, p. 8, identifies the Lee–Gauduchon cone with the dual of classes ρ whose ordinary Bott–Chern class dᶜρ is pseudoeffective. It does not establish that every LCK Lee class belongs to this latter cone. That membership is precisely the conjectural step, after the explicit sign translation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.05595))

notes.summary: Twisted Bott–Chern vanishing is not P03; for the explicitly defined weight connection d−λ, the normalized Chern class is 2{κλ}.
notes.detailedSummary: The older Morse–Novikov paper’s “Bott–Chern class of the LCK-manifold” is [ω] with coefficients in the weight local system, not the ordinary class {κλ}. The 2018 weighted paper also concerns coefficient bundles. A direct calculation for D=d−λ, with its (0,1) holomorphic structure and a unit smooth frame, gives F=−4πiκλ and iF/(2π)=2κλ. Dualizing the weight bundle reverses this sign.
notes.text:
Opened primary source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/0712.0107, Ornea–Verbitsky, “Morse–Novikov cohomology of locally conformally Kähler manifolds,” inspected version 3, March 26, 2008. Section 2.1, pp. 7–8, defines the weight connection D=d−θ and its holomorphic structure from D⁰¹. Definition 4.4, p. 14, calls [ω]∈H¹¹_BC(M,L) the Bott–Chern class of the LCK manifold. This is a coefficient-valued class, not P03’s ordinary curvature class. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0712.0107))

Also opened: https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jmath/70/1/70_409/_pdf/-char/en, Ornea–Verbitsky–Vuletescu, “Weighted Bott–Chern and Dolbeault cohomology for LCK-manifolds with potential,” J. Math. Soc. Japan 70 (2018), 409–422. Section 4 and Proposition 4.1, pp. 419–420, concern Hᵖᑫ_BC(M,Lᵅ) and twisted differentials. They do not establish positivity of an ordinary Lee curvature class. ([jstage.jst.go.jp](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jmath/70/1/70_409/_pdf/-char/en))

Normalization calculation, independent of an imported curvature formula: choose a global smooth frame e with |e|=1 and D=d−λ. The holomorphic operator is bar∂_L=bar∂−λ⁰¹. Metric compatibility determines the Chern connection one-form A=λ¹⁰−λ⁰¹=4πiλᶜ_task. Thus F=dA=4πi dλᶜ_task=−4πiκλ, and the normalized real Chern form is iF/(2π)=2κλ. Equivalently, locally λ=df, the holomorphic frame s=eᶠe has squared norm e²ᶠ, yielding the same curvature.

Consequently, with this precisely specified weight bundle, ordinary pseudoeffectivity of c₁_BC(L) is equivalent to P03. The dual bundle, or the connection d+λ, represents −2{κλ}; its positivity would be the opposite assertion. A singular metric h·e⁻²ᵘ gives Chern current 2(κλ+ddᶜ_task u). Flatness of D does not make its Chern curvature Bott–Chern trivial. The older source’s printed curvature factor in Theorem 2.2 was not reconciled with its operator conventions and is not used as a numerical premise here.

notes.summary: An inspected June 2026 primary paper remains Vaisman-specific and does not extend pseudoeffectivity to unrestricted LCK manifolds.
notes.detailedSummary: Marchidanu’s 2026 Aubin–Yau paper treats transversally Kähler foliations and applications to Vaisman manifolds. Theorem 6.6 supplies the familiar Vaisman semipositive form. Theorem 6.12 additionally assumes a basic first-Chern-class equality for the weight bundle. Neither theorem provides a positive current for a general strict LCK Lee class.
notes.text:
Opened full publisher text: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10455-026-10049-0, Vlad Marchidanu, “An Aubin-Yau theorem for transversally Kähler foliations,” Annals of Global Analysis and Geometry 70, article 3 (2026). Received August 28, 2025; accepted June 2, 2026; published June 15, 2026. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10455-026-10049-0))

Theorem 6.6 assumes a Vaisman structure with |θ|=1 and states that ω₀=−dJθ is closed semipositive, with kernel the canonical foliation. Theorem 6.12 assumes Vaisman and c₁(L)=c₁(K_M⊗²) in basic cohomology. It obtains a new Vaisman metric with the same de Rham Lee class and Chern–Ricci form −ω₀′, unique up to a constant. Its proof applies the paper’s transverse Aubin–Yau theorem. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10455-026-10049-0))

These results are restricted, not P03. Their transverse/basic cohomology hypothesis must not be substituted for ordinary Bott–Chern pseudoeffectivity. The numerical convention for Jθ and ω₀ was not fully reconciled here, so this paper is not used as a normalized curvature premise.

notes.summary: Bounded search establishes no unrestricted proof or counterexample; the remaining target is positivity against every Gauduchon test for each prescribed LCK Lee class.
notes.detailedSummary: As of this October 13, 2026 search, the inspected primary texts explicitly retain the conjecture or impose special-class hypotheses. No complete unrestricted theorem or genuine counterexample was established. Publisher-final and author-site retrieval limitations prevent an exhaustive literature verdict. Search failure is not evidence that no theorem exists.
notes.text:
Outcome: this literature invocation does not establish a full theorem proving P03 and does not establish a compact strictly LCK counterexample. The decisive inspected primary papers explicitly retain the unrestricted assertion as a conjecture, while the later inspected primary result remains Vaisman-specific. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.04623))

The bounded search included exact combinations of locally conformally Kähler/LCK, Lee class, weight bundle, pseudoeffective/pseudo-effective, Ornea–Verbitsky, and 2025–2026. Retrieval limitations: https://doi.org/10.1093/imrn/rnaf014 did not yield the complete publisher-final article; Ornea’s linked public Drive viewer, https://drive.google.com/file/d/1gooWidMkEPqPqPBEe2XuUtYWd45Cb1fI/view?usp=drive_link, exposed only a viewer shell, and its direct-download attempt failed. https://verbit.ru/ and https://verbit.ru/papers/ also failed. Therefore no claim is made that every later publication or final-version correction was inspected. ([]())

Precise next mathematical target, using the task-granted duality: for every prescribed nonexact LCK Lee form λ, establish ∫_X κλ∧γⁿ⁻¹≥0 for every smooth positive γ satisfying ddᶜ_task(γⁿ⁻¹)=0; alternatively construct an actual such X, λ and test with a rigorously negative integral. A deformation strategy would need additional evidence covering arbitrary LCK structures and preserving or controlling the prescribed Lee class. Neither the known-example list nor one positive conformal-Gauduchon pairing supplies that missing quantifier.

full_task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of complex dimension n>=2 with a strictly locally conformally Kahler metric omega: d omega=lambda wedge omega and d lambda=0, where lambda is a smooth real nonexact one-form. Use d^c=(i/(4 pi))(barpartial-partial), dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial, and lambda^c=(i/(4 pi))(lambda^{0,1}-lambda^{1,0}). The smooth closed real (1,1)-form kappa_lambda=-d lambda^c is de Rham exact and defines an ordinary Bott-Chern class. A closed real (1,1) Bott-Chern class is pseudoeffective if it has a closed positive (1,1)-current representative, equivalently there is a genuine quasi-plurisubharmonic canonical representative u with kappa_lambda+dd^c u>=0. The claim is invariant under conformal changes omega->exp(a)omega, which replace lambda by lambda+d a and kappa_lambda by kappa_lambda-dd^c a.

Original P03 conjectures that {kappa_lambda} is pseudoeffective for EVERY such compact strictly LCK manifold. Its pairing with the conformal Gauduchon representative of the LCK metric is strictly positive, and Vaisman/Hopf examples have a semipositive representative; these are background, not the full assertion. Lamari duality relates pseudoeffectivity to nonnegative pairing with EVERY smooth positive Gauduchon test gamma^{n-1}, dd^c(gamma^{n-1})=0. Positivity against one test does not prove the conjecture. Prove the unrestricted conjecture or construct an actual compact strictly LCK counterexample. No candidate proof, construction or auxiliary claim is supplied.
full_task.completionCriteria: A full proof for arbitrary compact strictly LCK manifolds, with all exact external premises checked against primary sources and the entire argument independently reconstructed, or an explicit compact strictly LCK counterexample with rigorously established failure of pseudoeffectivity (for example a rigorously negative Gauduchon pairing). A restricted Vaisman, Hopf, potential or surface case, positivity against only the LCK-induced test, the already known balanced obstruction, or an additional assumption equivalent to the target does not resolve P03. Retain ordinary Bott-Chern cohomology and the stated normalizations; de Rham exactness does not imply Bott-Chern triviality.
